stem: Which of the following is a suitable treatment option for otitis externa when the ear canal is markedly oedematous?

options.text: Syringe the ear canal with water to clean out debris
Take a swab of the discharge and commence topical antibiotic drops
Place an otowick in the canal to allow topical drops to reach the infected skin
In mild cases, start oral antibiotics first, as this is more effective than topical antibiotic drops
Give one or two doses of oral steroid

explanation: Otitis externa is usually treated with topical therapy. If canal swelling is severe, an otowick can be inserted to improve delivery of drops. Ear syringing is not appropriate in acute otitis externa, oral antibiotics are usually not first-line, and oral steroids are not standard treatment.
rationale: The original item is multiple-answer; it is rewritten into a single-best-answer question using the clearest correct management option.

optionExplanations.A: Ear syringing can worsen pain and trauma in acute otitis externa.
optionExplanations.B: A swab may be taken if discharge is present, but topical drops alone are not the best single answer here.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: an otowick helps topical treatment reach the canal when oedema is severe.
optionExplanations.D: Oral antibiotics are not usually preferred for uncomplicated otitis externa.
optionExplanations.E: Oral steroids are not routine treatment for otitis externa.
